text: Soil preparation (ការរៀបចំដី / ការភ្ជួរដី) for a Preah Vihear smallholder should match the field to the crop, rainfall, and available water rather than aiming to make soil as fine or loose as possible. Rice (ស្រូវ), cassava (ដំឡូងមី), and cashew (ស្វាយចន្ទី) are the main crops in the province. Before preparing a field, check whether the soil is sandy, clayey, or red soil, whether the land is low or elevated, how well it drains, and how water behaves in the wet season (រដូវវស្សា, roughly May-October) versus dry season (រដូវប្រាំង, roughly November-April). During the wet season, excessive tillage on sloping or exposed land increases erosion and runoff, so retaining crop residues and avoiding unnecessary soil disturbance helps. During the dry season, avoid preparing more land than can be reliably planted or irrigated. For rice, leveling and puddling may be appropriate where the system depends on retaining water; this differs from preparing well-drained upland soil for cassava or cashew. Soil fertility varies substantially among Cambodia's local soil groups, so fertilizer should ideally be based on actual soil conditions rather than a universal recommendation. A laboratory soil test may not be affordable or accessible to every smallholder -- where testing is unavailable, rely on observable soil characteristics (the field 'ribbon test': sandy soil crumbles and won't hold a rope shape; loamy soil rolls into a rope that cracks when bent into a ring; clay soil rolls smooth and bends into a ring without cracking) rather than guessing a specific soil type for an individual, unverified field.
